question: Which chamber of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary circulation?
explanation: The right ventricle collects blood from the right atrium and forces it through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk for transport to the lungs. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h1)

question: Why is the pulmonary circulation described as a low-pressure system compared to the systemic circulation?

options.A: Lungs require very high resistance to function properly
options.B: Deoxygenated blood is naturally lighter than oxygenated blood
options.C: It only needs to pump blood a short distance to the lungs
options.D: The heart beats much slower during pulmonary circulation

explanation: Because the lungs sit right next to the heart, the pulmonary vessels do not need high pressure to push blood through them. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h1)

question: What is unique about the blood carried inside the pulmonary arteries?
explanation: Pulmonary arteries are unique because they carry oxygen-poor blood away from the heart toward the lungs, unlike systemic arteries. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h2)

question: Name the vessel that directly divides to supply the left and right lungs.
explanation: The pulmonary trunk emerges from the right ventricle and splits into the left and right pulmonary arteries. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h2)

question: What physical process moves oxygen from the alveoli into the pulmonary capillaries?
explanation: Gases move naturally across the alveolar-capillary membrane from an area of higher concentration to lower concentration without using cellular energy. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h3)

question: Which of the following describes the movement of carbon dioxide during pulmonary gas exchange?

options.A: From the capillaries into the alveoli
options.B: From the bronchial tree into the heart
options.C: From the alveoli into the pulmonary veins
options.D: From the left atrium into the lungs

explanation: Carbon dioxide waste is dropped off by the blood into the air sacs so it can leave the body when the patient breathes out. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h3)

question: Which heart chamber receives oxygenated blood directly from the pulmonary veins?
explanation: The pulmonary veins empty freshly oxygenated blood straight into the left atrium, which then passes it to the left ventricle. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h4)

question: A midwife is reviewing fetal circulation versus adult circulation. Which vessels in the adult pulmonary circuit carry oxygenated blood?
explanation: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood back from the lungs to the heart, unlike all other veins in the body. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h4)

question: What does the term PVR stand for in cardiovascular physiology?
explanation: PVR stands for pulmonary vascular resistance, representing the force opposing blood flow through the lungs. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h5)

question: How do small pulmonary blood vessels react when an area of the lung has very low oxygen levels?
explanation: Hypoxic vasoconstriction causes local vessels to narrow so blood is sent to healthier parts of the lung where oxygen is available. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h5)

question: Which chamber of the heart suffers the most strain when pulmonary vascular resistance remains chronically high?
explanation: High resistance in the lungs forces the right ventricle to pump harder against high pressure, which can lead to right heart failure or cor pulmonale. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h6)

question: Which condition describes right-sided heart failure caused by long-term disorders of the pulmonary circulation?
explanation: Cor pulmonale is enlargement and failure of the right ventricle resulting from chronic pulmonary hypertension or lung disease. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h6)
